inspiration.observed_pattern: A catalog query computes multiple conditional counts from one filtered relation, separating rows where a timestamp is NULL from rows where it is present while retaining an unconditional count.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original support-team and incident-events scenario. PostgreSQL COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...) expressions become SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) and COUNT(CASE WHEN ... THEN event_id END); the fixture adds a LEFT JOIN, grouped teams, a NULL-extended team, and an independent event status/priority combination without copying the source schema or rows.

fixture_notes: Team 10 has one open high-priority event and one closed low-priority event; team 20 has two open events with only one high-priority event; team 30 has no events and exercises the NULL-extended join row; event 99 belongs to an unknown team and must not contribute to any team aggregate.
determinism_notes: The grouped read is ordered by the unique team ID and contains no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE support_teams (team_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE incident_events (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_id INT NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, priority VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT t.team_id, t.team_name, COUNT(e.event_id) AS total_events, SUM(CASE WHEN e.status = 'open' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_events, SUM(CASE WHEN e.status = 'closed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_events, COUNT(CASE WHEN e.priority = 'high' THEN e.event_id END) AS high_priority_events FROM support_teams t LEFT JOIN incident_events e ON e.team_id = t.team_id GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name ORDER BY t.team_id
